document.abstract: The AAF Association introduces the AAF Edit Protocol, a companion to the Advanced Authoring Format Specification, and the AAF Developer's Toolkit. The goal of the AAF Edit Protocol is to provide users with the most reliable mechanism for interchange of complex program metadata. Designed to codify best practices for the storage and exchange of program metadata in AAF files, the Edit Protocol defines constraints to the AAF Specification in order to achieve maximal interoperability of rich edit metadata. The Edit Protocol is the result of contributions from AAF Association member companies and builds on their experience implementing AAF in real products.

authors.bio: Ed McDermid is head of marketing for BBC Technology's North American operations, and serves on the AAF Association Board of Directors. He brings a broad depth of knowledge in large-scale digital media production and collaboration facilities, complex media asset management, broadcast, and web-based content distribution strategies, and e-commerce. Primary areas of focus include solutions for post-production, enhanced television production and distribution, and content repurposing across print, broadcast, PC and other internet devices. Prior to the BBC, McDermid served as the senior product manager for the Amazon.com Anywhere Group, responsible for product planning, feature requirements, user testing, product strategy, competitive analysis, and financial tracking for Amazon's award-winning non-PC platforms including WAP, PDA, and Interactive TV. Before joining Amazon, McDermid was with Avid Technology; responsible for driving the development partner programs based on Avid's OMF, AAF, and OMM interoperability initiatives. While at Avid he participated in standards efforts including SMPTE, AES, ISO, MPEG, and the EBU/SMPTE taskforce.
